$comment: The differential scenarios for `agentic.skill.validate`. One file, read by both implementations: `scenarios/lib/skill.mjs` drives `Package/skill-contract`, `Crate/SkillContract/Test/Parity.rs` drives the Rust port, and both answer the same `expect` block. Unlike `browser-cdp.json` this capability reads a real filesystem, so a scenario describes a corpus - a tree of files - and each side builds that tree in its own temporary directory before the port runs. The tree is described by `fixture`: `corpus` (one skill directory each: `name` is the directory name, `frontmatter` is the text between the fences of `SKILL.md`, `references` are files under `Reference/`, `referenceIndex` is `Reference/Index.md`, `cited` (default true) decides whether the corpus root's index names it, `noBody` leaves the directory without a `SKILL.md`), `symlink` (one more skill, written outside the corpus root and linked in by name), `corpusIndex` (`Index.md`, `AGENTS.md` or null, its text generated from the `cited` flags), `rootFiles` (files at the root, which are not skills), `absentRoot` (the root does not exist) and `touchAfterFirstValidate` (a path written under the first validated skill after that call returns). The steps are `discover`; `validate <skill>` (discover, then validate that record); `validateDiscovered <skill>` (validate the record the last discover answered, so no second discover happens); `digest` (the last discovered records, a literal `skills` list, or that list with one `mutate` - `{reverse: true}` or `{at, ...fields}` - applied); and `touch` (push every file's modification time a day forward). `effects` is what the port reported, in order: `discovered:<name>` for every skill a discover answered and `finding:<rule>:<skill>` for every finding a validate reported, so a port that answered the same findings in a different order, or discovered twice where the scenario says once, fails. `digest` and `touch` have no effects. Every digest is asserted as an exact constant, never as a pattern: the recorded `sha256:86b8b052...` is the one both contract suites already record, and the other constants are the values both ports must agree on for the corpora described here. The one thing this file cannot see is a finding's `detail`: the shared comparison in `scenarios/lib/load.mjs` compares a `findings` result by rule, so detail wording stays with the two contract suites. See `Documentation/Parity.md` for the case map.
